issues.legal_issue: Changing the business conducted in premises leased for business purposes does not constitute a change of user warranting eviction when the new business is suitable for the premises and causes no damage, impairment, or nuisance.
material_facts: The tenant leased a shop under a rent note specifying an English liquor business.
After the liquor licence was not renewed, the tenant discontinued that business and began selling general merchandise in the shop.
The shop continued to be used for business, and the new business could conveniently be carried on there without impairing the shop’s utility, damaging it, or creating a nuisance.
The landlord sought eviction on the ground that the tenant had changed the use of the shop.
The tenant tendered the rent arrears at the first hearing; the issue decided on appeal was the alleged change of user.
issues.conclusion: The change from a liquor business to general merchandise did not constitute a change of user attracting the statutory eviction ground. The appeal was allowed and the eviction order was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 13(2)(ii)(b) of the Haryana Urban (Control of Rent and Eviction) Act, 1973, a tenant may be evicted for using premises for a purpose other than that for which they were leased. Whether a different business amounts to a different purpose must be assessed in light of the rent legislation’s purpose and the circumstances, including whether the new use impairs the premises or creates a nuisance. The rule that only allied businesses can avoid being a change of user, stated by the Punjab and Haryana High Court in Sikander Lal v. Amrit Lal, must be read with reservation. Maharaj Kishan Kesar v. Milkha Singh treated an allied business as not constituting a change of user. In interpreting legislation, the meaning of an expression is to be found in the felt necessities of the time; the Court referred to Duport Steels Ltd. v. Sirs on the judicial role in interpreting legislation.

rule.if: rent_eviction_proceeding and premises_leased_for_business and tenant_used_premises_for_different_business and new_business_suited_to_premises and no_impairment_or_damage and no_nuisance

predicates.rent_eviction_proceeding: A landlord brought a proceeding seeking eviction of a tenant from rented premises.
predicates.premises_leased_for_business: The premises were leased for the purpose of carrying on a business.
predicates.tenant_used_premises_for_different_busin: The tenant conducted a business different from the one specified when the premises were leased.
predicates.new_business_suited_to_premises: The different business could conveniently be carried on in the premises.
predicates.no_impairment_or_damage: The different business did not impair the utility of or damage the premises.
predicates.no_nuisance: The tenant’s different business created no nuisance.
predicates.different_business_not_change_of_user_gr: The different business does not establish a change-of-user ground for eviction.

issues.definition: When a tenant facing an eviction proceeding changes from one business to another in premises leased for business, and the new business suits the premises without impairment, damage, or nuisance, the change does not establish the change-of-user ground.
